Pied-à-terre tax · For buildings

Building summaries for managing agents, boards and accountants

How the pied-à-terre surcharge falls on one building, from public city records, without owners or unit values.

When the surcharge notices and bills arrive, owners ask their managing agent, their board or their accountant the same questions: is our building affected, how many units, how did the city get these values, and what can we do before March 1? A building summary answers those for one building on one or two pages, from public city records. The free building pages on this site show the headline counts; the summary adds the detail below.

What is in a building summary

  • The building in the city's records: units on the FY2027 roll, how many are valued at $1 million or more, and the spread of city values.
  • Units by bracket and units near a line: how many sit within 10% below or above $1, $3 and $5 million. These are the units where a value question matters.
  • For co-ops: the share of the stock at which an apartment crosses each line, so the board can read it against its own share schedule.
  • Recorded sales (condos): deed sales since 2023, the median price, and how far the city's value sits below it.
  • How the city valued the building: DOF's latest published income, expenses and comparable rental buildings.
  • A board and agent checklist for the January 1 bills and the March 1, 2027 TC107 deadline, and what changes in July 2028.

It never lists owners, apartment numbers or unit-by-unit values, and it does not suggest what value anyone should claim. It reports public records and is not legal or tax advice.

One full sample, so you can see what you get: 1 West End Avenue (condominium), 2 pages. A co-op summary has the same parts, with the share thresholds in place of the sales section, in one or two pages. Summaries for other buildings are only available to order.

Who uses it

  • Managing agents who need one clear explanation to send to every owner in a building.
  • Co-op and condo boards. A co-op corporation may file a TC107 for a unit owner.
  • Accountants and wealth managers with clients who own in New York City.

Price and ordering

  • One building: $149. One fee covers the whole building, instead of each owner buying a $79 unit report.
  • Five or more buildings: $99 each. For managing agents and accountants with several buildings.

Pay securely through Stripe and enter the building address at checkout. I email the PDF, usually within one business day (two for five or more). If an address matches more than one building, I write to check first. See the refund policy.
